processing_steps.method: centrifugal casting under near-rapid solidification (copper mould)
processing_steps.heating_or_cooling_rate: calculated maximum cooling rate about 5×10^3 K/s
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingot made from high purity Fe (99.99%), Mn (99.9%), Al (99.9%), C (99.8%), and Cr (99.9%); ingot reheated to melt by an induction coil, then liquid metal poured into a copper mold at a rotating speed of 600 r/min in Ar atmosphere; obtained strip size (60–80) mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm.

Some near-rapidly solidified strips were heat-treated in a vacuum electric resistance furnace; annealing at 550 °C for 5 h was applied to all four Cr-containing alloys (0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr, 9Cr) to compare with the as-cast state. Cooling medium not specified.

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase austenite (γ) + ferrite (δ) microstructure; austenite is the major matrix phase and δ-ferrite is uniformly dispersed as block-like particles. After annealing at 550 °C for 5 h the constituent phases remain austenite and ferrite, and the size and fraction of ferrite almost remain the same as the as-cast strip.
structures.number_of_phases: 2 (austenite γ + ferrite δ), plus nano-scale DO3 ordered domains in ferrite and weak κ-carbide superlattice

phases_present.crystal_structure: FCC (austenite lattice constant 3.56 Å for 6Cr from XRD by JADE)

phases_present.morphology: κ-carbide superlattice in SADP of annealed 6Cr still very weak (precipitation suppressed by Cr); sizes too small to identify

defects.dislocation_density: dislocation density in austenite of annealed Cr-containing strips obviously reduced compared with as-cast Cr-containing strips, but still higher than that of annealed 0Cr strip (no numeric value given)

precipitates.distribution: in austenite matrix; superlattice reflections very weak in annealed 6Cr

microstructure_list.region: δ-ferrite particles dispersed in the austenite matrix

phases_present.volume_fraction: 14.8 vol% (as-cast 6Cr measurement; size and fraction almost unchanged after annealing)
phases_present.morphology: angular/block-like particles, becoming more irregular and branched in the annealed 6Cr SEM image; no resolvable grain boundary
nano-scale DO3 particles in ferrite; DF image (annealed 6Cr) shows a cigar/teardrop-shaped region filled with fine equiaxed grains under the 'δ+DO3' label

defects.dislocation_density: only a few dislocations occasionally observed in the ferrite of all strips

precipitates.distribution: in ferrite; present after annealing at 550 °C for 5 h in all strips including 6Cr

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Increase of δ-ferrite fraction in Cr-containing strips can block dislocation propagation due to more phase-interface areas, which may decrease plasticity.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Slip bands observed in austenite during deformation of the strips. After tensile fracture, the annealed 6Cr strip shows the finest, densest slip band set: average slip-band spacing ~60 nm and average slip-band width 7.9 nm. Smaller and less κ-carbides (relatively easy to cut through) allow multi-directional shearing, leading to narrow slip band spacing; annealing widens spacing in 0Cr (90→190 nm) but narrows it in 6Cr (80→60 nm).
interfaces.phase_evolution: Annealing at 550 °C for 5 h leaves austenite + ferrite unchanged; promotes κ-carbide precipitation but suppressed in Cr-containing strips (superlattice still very weak in 6Cr); DO3 ordering appears in ferrite of all annealed strips including 6Cr; dislocation density in austenite reduced compared with as-cast 6Cr but still higher than annealed 0Cr.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests by MTS Criterion Model 44 mechanical property tester with a 10 kN capacity; each test data supported by more than three tensile specimens; values averaged over 3 measurements (annealed at 550 °C for 5 h)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 8(a) engineering stress-strain curves of annealed strips: the 6Cr curve keeps rising past the 900 MPa gridline and extends furthest, close to the 50% strain gridline.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Increment of yield strength after annealing: +101 MPa; increment of total elongation after annealing: +12.7 % (annealed 6Cr strip vs as-cast 6Cr strip)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: D/Max-2200, Cu target, operated at 40 kV and 40 mA, scan rate 4° per min
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify constituent phases of the annealed strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Annealed 6Cr pattern shows only γ and δ reflections; the κ(111) reflection at ~41.4° is absent, confirming Cr suppresses κ-carbide precipitation even after annealing.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEM-2100F, operated at a voltage of 200 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: annealed at 550 °C for 5 h; DF images; SADP insets; 500 nm (200 nm in some panels) scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine dislocations, κ-carbide superlattice and DO3 ordering in austenite and ferrite of annealed strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Annealed 6Cr austenite SADP indexed along [1̄12]γ+[1̄12]κ with weak superlattice; dislocation density reduced vs as-cast but higher than annealed 0Cr; ferrite shows δ+DO3 with a cigar/teardrop region of fine equiaxed grains.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: annealed at 550 °C for 5 h; 20 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.key_findings: Annealed 6Cr strip shows a grey matrix with dispersed dark particles of more irregular, branched, skeleton-like outlines; no resolvable grain boundary (unlike annealed 0Cr).

characterization_methods.purpose: Observe ferrite distribution and morphology in the austenite matrix
characterization_methods.key_findings: Δ-ferrite uniformly distributes in the austenite matrix; 6Cr (as-cast) shows predominantly angular/block-like ferrite particles, more numerous and coarser than 3Cr.

characterization_methods.technique: Inductively Coupled Plasma mass spectrometry (ICP) and Electronic Water Displacement Density Analyzer
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ICP; SJ-600G Electronic Water Displacement Density Analyzer
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine actual strip composition and measured average density
characterization_methods.key_findings: 6Cr strip composition (wt.%): Fe Bal., Mn 29.1, Al 9.9, C 1.2, Cr 6.8; measured average density 6.46 g/cm^3.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: strain rate 1×10^-3 s^-1; gauge size 20 mm × 4 mm × 1 mm; annealed at 550 °C for 5 h; averaged over 3 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and total elongation
characterization_methods.key_findings: Annealed 6Cr strip: YS 751 ± 2 MPa, UTS 965 ± 2 MPa, TE 44.3 ± 3 %.

computational_details.simulation_method: Quantitative measurement of ferrite volume fraction from micrographs

analytical_models.model_note: quantitative measurement by Gatan Digital Micrograph; annealed ferrite fraction and size almost unchanged from as-cast

analytical_models.model_name: austenite lattice constant refinement from XRD
analytical_models.model_note: austenite lattice constant determined from XRD results by JADE

unmapped_findings: Measured (ICP) composition of the 6Cr strip (Table 1): Fe Bal., Mn 29.1, Al 9.9, C 1.2, Cr 6.8 wt.% (Cr close to the nominal 6 wt.% target).
Measured average density of the 6Cr strip is 6.46 g/cm^3 (density analyzer SJ-600G).

The total elongation of the annealed 6Cr strip (44.3 ± 3 %) is better than that of the annealed Cr-free (0Cr) strip; the 6Cr curve extends furthest in Fig. 8(a) engineering stress-strain (close to the 50 % gridline).

The strain hardening rate of the annealed strips is higher with increasing Cr content; the reduction in strain hardening rate of annealed 3Cr strip is the largest, about 500 MPa (no numeric value given specifically for annealed 6Cr).

Slip-band data for the annealed 6Cr strip after tensile fracture: average spacing ~60 nm and average width 7.9 nm; these accompany the highest ductility except for as-cast 6Cr (dynamic slip band refinement, DSBR).
As-cast 6Cr average steady-stage strain hardening rate is reported as 2266 MPa (as-cast state; corresponds to the parent as-cast sample, not the annealed condition of this sample).
